events.credibility_reason: The conjecture was stated false in the same OEIS entry (counterexamples n = 364, 1755, both composite index).

Specific unanswered objection: the key section 4.2 formula fails for p = 1093, n = 2 and the postulate fails for any Wieferich prime; the argument itself is unreadable and the problem is still listed open.
OEIS comments say earlier PrimeGrid results were not double-checked; no double-check of the December 2022 run found.

why: Nothing in the record settles or bounds the universal question. The Warren–Bray, Shevelev and Laniewski items are reductions or reformulations (none). The Wieferich searches, Gallardo's Sophie Germain check and Caldwell's q < 1213 factorization check are finite verifications (instances); a Wieferich-prime search bound could be read as a bound, but the statement asks a yes/no question with no quantity, so it only narrows where a counterexample could hide. Caldwell's 1213 claim cannot be dated relative to the snapshot (null), but it is instances either way. Basaldúa's 2001 claimed full proof is knocked down by a specific, unanswered objection to its key step. Jovovic's conjecture concerns all n (variant) and was refuted at composite indices. Wagstaff and Kovač–Luca address different questions about Mersenne numbers (variant). No AI involvement anywhere.
doubts: The IJCS paper was seen only in search excerpts, with no date or authors confirmed. The Basaldúa knock-down rests on a reader's reported objection, because the argument itself could not be read.
